transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've been having trouble sleeping for about three months now, ever since I retired. I feel exhausted all day and it's really getting me down.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
No, I don't have any allergies to medicines that I know of.
How much does your trouble sleeping affect your day-to-day life?
It's a big problem, honestly. I'm too tired to get out and work on my allotment like I used to, and I keep dozing off in the chair in the afternoon. It's frustrating.
Could you tell me what medicines you take, including any new or recently changed ones?

I take losartan for my blood pressure, 50 milligrams once a day. And tamsulosin at night for my prostate, 400 micrograms. I've also been taking some over-the-counter sleeping tablets from the pharmacy most nights for the last three weeks.
Have you ever had any operations?
No, I've never had any operations.
Where do you experience the trouble sleeping?
I'm not sure what you mean by where — it's at night, in my bed at home. I live alone, so there's no one else being disturbed by it.
Is there anything that seems to make your sleep better or worse?
If I've had a late evening watching telly, it seems worse. On days when I've been out for a good long walk, I tend to sleep better.
Is there anything else you've noticed along with the sleep trouble that you'd like to add?
My mood has been a bit low at times since I retired, though I've not had any thoughts of harming myself. That's about it, really.
What is it like for you when you’re in bed at night and having trouble sleeping?
I just can't get off to sleep at all at night. It's really frustrating lying there.
Is there anything else about your past health you’d like to add?
Nothing else I can think of. The blood pressure and the prostate trouble are the main things, and both are managed with the tablets I mentioned.
How much would you say the trouble getting off to sleep is affecting your day-to-day life — not at all, a little, or a lot, or are you not sure?

It affects me a lot — I'd put it at about a 7 out of 10. And actually, I should correct myself from earlier: I do nod off fine at about 11 pm, but then I wake at 3 or 4 in the morning and can't get back to sleep. That's the real problem.

Earlier you said you can’t get off to sleep at all, and then you said you fall asleep fine at about 11 but wake at 3 or 4 and can’t get back to sleep — which of those is closer to what you’re experiencing?
The second one is right — I fall asleep fine at about 11 pm, but I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning and can't get back to sleep. I got that muddled earlier.
Have any of your medicines been started or changed recently — say in the last few weeks or months — or have they stayed about the same, or are you not sure?
The losartan and tamsulosin have stayed the same for a good while. The only new thing is those over-the-counter sleeping tablets I started from the pharmacy about three weeks ago.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
